answer: Sybil farms pay only while extra identities stay cheap, so each epoch the chain derives fresh words from a seed nobody can preview, and every agent must answer them alone. Reusing an old fable fails: the ledger hashes each response and refuses duplicates, so a thousand socks must fund a thousand distinct generations. That basalt-hard per-identity cost is checked by peers, so an attacker cannot quietly forge a crowd of verifiers; every extra voice still pays the same inference price, leaving fake consensus stranded on the reef and its expected return below honest work.
